KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and unseasonably mild conditions continue
through Saturday night. 

High pressure centered over the central Appalachians will move
over New England Saturday, reaching the North Atlantic south of
the Maritimes by Saturday evening. Dry weather will prevail
during this time with light winds for most of it. Wind direction
shifts from the west, to more of a SE to S wind by Saturday
afternoon.

Followed the persistence trend of drier air leading to high
temperatures closer to the highest guidance, as well as closest
to the lowest guidance at night. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...

A period of heavy rain, gusty winds, and coastal flooding continue 
to be likely late Sunday into Monday as a coastal low tracks near 
southern New England. 

Sunday into early next week, a mid-level trough shifts across the 
Great Lakes region lowering heights across the northeast, allowing 
the progressive coastal low to track up the coastline near southern 
New England. Trends continue to show general agreement across 
deterministic and ensemble guidance in the pattern and the track of 
the low with recent guidance showing eastward trend in track. A 
plume of above normal moisture, 280-330 percent of normal, surges 
northward ahead of the approaching trough and coastal low. This will 
prime the environment for heavy rainfall once the better 
forcing/instability arrive with the incoming coastal low. There is 
still a degree of variance in the low tracks across solutions which 
may have impact on the finer details(gust magnitude, rain totals). 
Ensembles continue to show potential for a swath of 1-3" possible 
across southern New England. The placement of the swath of higher 
amounts will depend on the exact track of the system. Ensembles and 
deterministic guidance show the swatch oriented from SW-NE central 
and western CT upwards to northeast MA. There is more variance 
across deterministic guidance with the RRFS showing a more east 
placement of this swatch across far west CT into RI and southeast 
MA. So still details to be ironed out on the placement of the 
highest amounts. Marginal instability combined with deep moisture 
will support an environment for heavy rain rates. This usually flags 
the risk for flash flooding; however, the progressive nature of
the system likely will limit this potential. A low/marginal 
risk for localized flash flooding can't be ruled out especially 
flood prone or poor drainage areas. This matches up with the WPC
ERO. The bulk of the rain likely exits by mid-morning Monday 
with the peak window for rainfall Sunday night/early Monday AM. 

The coastal low will carry a strong pressure gradient supporting 
gusty winds. Magnitude of the winds/gusts will also depend on the 
strength and track of the low. The ECMWF ensemble shows 
probabilities of 40-60% for gusts 34 kts or greater across the 
southern and eastern coastal waters Sunday night into Monday 
morning. As for the land, gusts 20-30 mph are possible with a risk 
for gusts 30-45 mph for the south coast and Cape/Islands. Strong 
gusts likely diminish across the coastal waters later Monday, 
although we'll have to watch for another push of gusty winds Tuesday 
with the cold front. 

We are continuing to monitor the potential for coastal flooding with 
increasing astro tides. Splashover to minor coastal flooding looks 
more likely at this time. 

Dry and cool conditions Tuesday into Wednesday with highs in the 40s 
and upper 30s for the higher terrain. High pressure should likely 
set us up for clear skies and efficient radiational cooling. This 
will result in chilly nights. Temperatures likely drop into the 20s 
Tuesday night, potentially upper teens in the higher elevation 
spots. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Potential for another system to bring mainly rain 
and wind sometime Wednesday night into Thanksgiving. Low risk for a 
snow/ice mix at the onset in the higher elevations. 

Model guidance continues to signal for another system to impact the 
region sometime Wed night into Thanksgiving. At this time, rain will 
likely be the dominate precipitation type.  Will have to keep an eye 
on the finer timing of as there will be a low risk for a bit of 
snow/ice at the onset across the interior if it is cold enough. 
Certainly something to watch give Holiday Travel...But overall this 
mainly looks like a rain event for most areas of southern New 
England.
